rv.q: Molly Sweeney is so carefully understated as it proceeds on its determined course that even viewers with 20/20 eyesight may not notice that its encouragement to acknowledge “blindsight” includes a moving one that whispers, “See this play about sight and its many underappreciated manifestations.
Not Much to See, but a Lot to Listen to, in Molly Sweeney: Brian Friel's play about a woman who regains her sight gets a Keen Company revival.
All in all, this production sails across the surface of the tale, when what Mr. Friel offered was a chance to go deep.

cn.t: Brian Friel's quietly powerful meditation on sight and blindness receives mixed reviews in Keen Company's revival, with praise for its evocative prose but criticism for its low-action storytelling approach.
